inline_hook <- function(x, digits=2){

  if(is.list(x)){
    x <- unlist(x)
  }
  if(is.numeric(x)){
      paste(format(x,big.mark=',',
                   digits=digits, nsmall=digits, scientific=FALSE))
  } else {
      paste(x)
  }
}
knitr::knit_hooks$set(inline=inline_hook)

package_version <- function(package){

  paste(unlist(packageVersion(package)), collapse='.')

}


oxford_comma <- function(x, digits=2) {

  x <- map_chr(x, inline_hook, digits=digits)

  if(length(x) < 2){
    x
  } else if(length(x) == 2){
    paste(x, collapse = " and ")
  } else {
    paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse=", "), x[length(x)], sep=", and ")
  }
}

  pretty = c("Postitive", "Negative", "Overlap",
             "CRC", "Sleep apnea", "Sponges")
)

## Introduction

* AND - Problem of uneven sampling effort and how to control for the effects
  * Previous work from me has show rarefaction controls for sampling effort 
  better than other methods
  * BUT - Confusion over difference between rarefaction and rarefying
  * THEREFORE - Define rarefaction

* AND - Critiques against rarefaction include
  * Compresses the alpha and beta diversity metrics
  * Perceived as "throwing away" data
  * Arbitrary choice for rarefaction threshold
  * BUT - these really aren't problems; largely unavoidable
  * THEREFORE - Use rarefaction

* AND - Additional problem with 16S rRNA gene sequencing is that the data are compositional
  * Define compositionality
  * Solutions to problem of compositionality
  * BUT - Still have sensitivity to uneven sampling effort
  * THEREFORE - Question of why I found different results from proponents of CLR-based methods

* AND - RPCA as a solution
  * Describe RPCA
  * Claims made by Martino
  * Methods used in Martino
  * BUT - Problems with analysis including not using rarefaction, arbitrary threshold selection, not using other CLR-based methods
  * THEREFORE - The goal of this study was to reassess RPCA using the framework and methods used by Martino et al. alongside other methods commonly used by microbial ecologists

* Other...
  * RPCA -> deicode -> gemelli
  * Benchmarking data and code forked from deicode




* Problems with original analysis
  * Simulation design
    * 1 seed to generate simulated communities
    * Null model had no skew to it
    * Simulated communities had uneven sampling effort

  * Choice of distance metrics for comparison
    * Compared RPCA to MatrixCompletion without using RCLR. Who would do this? Why not at least also compare to CLR w/ a pseudocount?

  * kNN
    * Used 1st 2 axes of PCoA of Bray-Curtis distances to calcualte euclidean distances, which were then fed into kNN. Why not use the original Bray-Curtis distance matrix?
    * 1 60:40 split (said 10-fold, but only repeated knn 10 times, not parititioning), did not fit hyperparameter; choice for case studies was messed up

  * Comparison of PERMANOVA Fst values misleading since they removed all of the noise by only considering first two axes from RPCA and comparing to PERMANOVA on original Bray-Curtis distances

  * Case study analysis
    * Picked case studies with large effect sizes that are easily seen on PCoA/PCA; most microbiome studies are not so easy to differentiate
    * Thresholds for subsampling case study datasets are arbitrary

  * Overall method problems
    * Choice of number of partitions/axes seems arbitrary/no guidance. Controls and sponges used 2, sleep apnea used 3. Default is 3, also auto_rpca available within recent implementation
  
  * Analysis of sequencing depth sensitivity was qualitative when quantitative methods are available
